source.anchor_kjv: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint: my heart is like wax; it is melted in the midst of my bowels. My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; and thou hast brought me into the dust of death. For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet. I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me.
source.thread: David describes a crucified body centuries before Rome crucified anyone - poured out like water, joints pulled loose, bones counted and stared at
source.hook_line: A king described a dying body so exactly it reads like an eyewitness account of a crucifixion he never saw.
source.spoken_script: A king described a dying body so exactly it reads like an eyewitness account of a crucifixion he never saw. Psalm twenty-two. David wrote it in the first person, but he was describing someone else's death, not his own. Watch the body of the dying man: "I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint " Drained and every joint pulled loose, the way a body hangs when it's suspended by the arms. And: "I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me." He could count every bone, stretched and exposed, while onlookers stood and stared at him. David never saw a crucifixion. Rome would not make it its instrument for centuries. Yet the dying man of his song bears the marks of one written early. This is what Jesus bore to bring you home every wrenched joint, every cold stare, recorded centuries early so you'd know none of it was chance. He was crushed in your place.

platforms.description:
A king described a dying body so exactly it reads like an eyewitness account of a crucifixion he never saw (Psalm 22:14-17).

"I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint" (Psalm 22:14, KJV). Drained, every joint pulled loose, the way a body hangs when it is suspended by the arms.

"I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me" (Psalm 22:17, KJV). Every bone stretched and exposed, while onlookers stood and stared.

David wrote it in the first person, but he was describing someone else's death. He never saw a crucifixion; Rome would not make it its instrument for centuries. Yet the dying man of his song bears the marks of one, written early.

This is what Jesus bore to bring you home: every wrenched joint, every cold stare, recorded centuries early so you would know none of it was chance. He was crushed in your place. Come home to him.

redteam:
VERDICT: PASS

- KJV check: both quoted fragments are verbatim ("I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint" - Psalm 22:14; "I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me" - Psalm 22:17), quote-marked and attributed at the point of quotation on every platform that quotes them, refs front-loaded. PASS.
- Historical honesty: the kit keeps the video's precise scoping - "Rome would not make it its instrument for centuries" - and never claims crucifixion was unknown before Rome. The "reads like an eyewitness account" hook carries the video's own "reads like" hedge. No overclaim.
- Restraint check (verified): the anchor range includes v16 ("they pierced my hands and my feet") but the video never quotes it, and the kit correctly does not lead with it or claim it. Right call - do not add it in any future edit.
- tiktok (minor, non-blocking): "Poured out like water, bones out of joint, counted and stared at" compresses KJV language without quote marks. It reads as summary allusion beside the named psalm, not as a quotation; acceptable at caption length.
- Titles: "A King Described a Death He Never Saw" is honest (David wrote ten centuries before the event) and does not collide with the sibling "The Crucifixion Foretold". No clickbait.
- Grace check: "He was crushed in your place. Come home to him" extends the video's own "to bring you home" landing; invitation, no fear or gain-loss framing. PASS.
